origins.section: A One-Row LP Is Solved by Sorting: Dantzig's Bound
Fixing an Item Changes the Budget, Not the Order
The Search Is a Stack of Fixings

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-dantzig: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-dantzig: fill the budget in that order: take each item whole while it fits, and take the fraction of the first item that does not fit that uses up what is left. (A 12 + B 10 + 1/3 of C = 1 gives 23.)
recorded.prompt:q-fixings: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-fixings: Its LP is the same fill with two changes: the items fixed at 1 are paid for first (whatever their ratio), and the items fixed at 0 are skipped. The free items keep their ratio order, so the list is sorted once, at the start, and never again.
recorded.prompt:q-relaxed-plan: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-relaxed-plan: That is the relaxation at work: this plan funds both P006 and P007, which are alternatives, and the knapsack has no row to stop it.

recorded.prompt:q-dantzig:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-dantzig:a: take the fraction of the first item that does not fit that uses up what is left. C is not left out.
recorded.prompt:q-dantzig:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-dantzig:b: since the fill obeys the row and the bounds 0 \le x_i \le 1, it is the LP optimum. The bound never breaks the budget.
recorded.prompt:q-dantzig:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-dantzig:c: take each item whole while it fits. B (cost 5) fits whole in the 6 left.
recorded.prompt:q-fixings:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-fixings:a: the list is sorted once, at the start, and never again. Filling as at the root also ignores that items fixed at 1 are paid for first.
recorded.prompt:q-fixings:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-fixings:c: Fixing an Item Changes the Budget, Not the Order ... The same three values to the last digit printed, from a loop over a sorted list instead of an LP solver.
recorded.prompt:q-fixings:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-fixings:d: the items fixed at 1 are paid for first (whatever their ratio), and the items fixed at 0 are skipped. The fixings come first; nothing is swapped afterwards.

recorded.prompt:q-relaxed-plan:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-relaxed-plan:c: Node 4 skips P004 and the fill is whole ... worth 3,021, the first incumbent. The plan comes from an integral node ("The integral case takes the LP solution as the new plan"), not from rounding.
